## TL;DR

The close-out clock was starting at enqueue time, not at validation start. The server snapshot used the job's `enqueuedAt` as the active start whenever the head job had not started yet, and the phase clock inherited it. A queued head job was therefore shown as the active close-out, with an elapsed time measured from when it was queued. The fix makes a job "active" only once it has left the queue (its `startedAt` is set), lists unstarted jobs in the queue with their position, and stops any timer from counting before that point. The UI timer helpers now read only the validating start. Retried attempts restart from their own start because a retry resets the job to queued. The final scoped `repoos check` passed, including the remote validation gate. Earlier runs surfaced one real failure (the `mtd-cancel` expectation, now updated) and a sign-in browser failure that came from the worktree having no local build; after `bun run build` it passed.

## Work and rationale

The reported symptom was a Checks timer of about 20 minutes on a card that had only just started, with a queued card showing no clear state. I traced the clock through three layers.

1. `src/server/integration-status.ts` builds the pipeline snapshot. It took `live[0]` as the in-flight job and computed `startedAt = inFlight.startedAt ?? inFlight.enqueuedAt`. A job still in the `queued` phase has `startedAt` null, so this fallback made the clock run from enqueue. `phaseStartedAt` for a queued job is also its enqueue time, so the phase clock had the same problem.
2. `src/ui-app/src/lib/closeOutAttempt.ts` returned `queueEnqueuedAt` for queued tasks. That was intentional for #0741: a failure that predates the wait should count as stale. I kept that behaviour, but moved it into a separate helper, `closeOutFailureCutoff`, so no timer reads an enqueue time.
3. The shared helpers in `integration-pipeline-ui.ts` already return a null elapsed time when `startedAt` is null. Once the server stops inventing a start, the card and the status bar stop showing a clock for queued work without any change to them.

The orchestrator sets `startedAt` on the queued-to-syncing transition (`integration-orchestrator.ts`), so `startedAt` is the earliest point the job is really running. I used it as the "validating start" the task asks for rather than inventing a second marker.

Decisions:

- The active job is now the first job with `attemptIsExecuting` true. Queued jobs go into the queue list, with position numbers starting at 1, and the queue detail is built in both branches of the function. Previously the no-active branch returned no `queueDetail`.
- Queue chips now say "waited Nm" instead of "pos N · Nm" so the wait reads as a note, not a timer.
- When there is no active job but the queue is non-empty, the summary says "Queued — waiting for the next close-out to start" instead of "Close-out in progress".

## Approaches tried

I first considered keeping the queued head as `active` and suppressing its clock on the client. That is smaller, but the card's role logic would still classify a queued head as "active" and render "integrating · stage", so every consumer would need the same special case. Moving the head into the queue fixes this at the source, and the existing UI helpers already handle `active: null` with a queue.

The cost is that some existing snapshot tests used an unstarted job as `active`. Those fixtures were not describing reality, since a job in the `validating` phase always has a start. I updated them to start their jobs rather than weakening the assertions.

## Challenges and blockers

- The screenshot's "Checks 20m 29s" appears to come from the card's check-run or local check-slot clock (`cardChecksDisplay` in `TaskCard.vue`, using `handoffStatus.startedAt`, the check run's `startedAt` or the slot's `ageMs`), not from the close-out job. I did not confirm which of these produced the figure in the screenshot, because that needs a live run. My change fixes the close-out clock. If the Checks figure still runs long after this lands, that is a separate clock and should be investigated on a live run.
- `closeOutAttemptStartedAt` is used only for stale-failure detection on the card, not to display a timer. I kept the function name the task names and changed its behaviour, and added `closeOutFailureCutoff` for the staleness case.
- Running vitest from the repository root fails on `.vue` imports. The UI suite needs the UI config, so I ran the affected test files directly and the full scoped check covers the rest.
- I did not verify the queued and validating states in a headless browser. No declared shots were added, because the change is a text and state change that needs a fixture I would have had to invent. A human should look at the queued label in the pipeline summary.

## Key learnings

- A "started" field that falls back to an earlier timestamp hides the state it was meant to show. The fallback looked harmless because the field was always set in the common path, but it was the only path for a job waiting behind the lock. Future snapshot fields should be null until the thing they describe has happened.
- Staleness and timers are different questions. #0741 needed an enqueue time to judge stale failures, while the timer needed the validating start. Mixing them in one helper made the timer inherit the staleness rule.
- Three tests asserted the old behaviour (an unstarted job is active). They were correct for the code they were written against, so I changed them to describe a started job and kept their other assertions.

## Tests

- `src/ui-app/tests/close-out-timer-1272.test.ts` covers the three states with a fake clock: queued (position and no blocker clock), validating (the clock counts from the job's own start, not its enqueue), and retried (the retry is queued again and then restarts from its own start).
- `src/ui-app/tests/close-out-attempt.test.ts` covers the UI helpers for timer and staleness cutoff.
- `integration-snapshot-detail.test.ts` and `mtd-cancel.test.ts` were updated so their jobs have started; the cancel test now expects the next job to be queued, not active.
